tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[The Universal Covering of $\mathbb {RP}^n$]1. chC:C.24↗ ex:real-projective-spaces ↗ prop:uniqueness-smooth-quotients

The two-element group $\Gamma = \{ \pm 1\} $ acts smoothly, freely, and properly on $S^n$ by multiplication, and thus $S^n/\Gamma $ is a smooth manifold and the quotient map $\pi : S^n \to S^n/\Gamma $ is a two-sheeted smooth normal covering map. Note also that the quotient map $\mathbb {R}^{n+1} \to \mathbb {R}^{n+1}$ defined in Example C.18 restricts to a surjective smooth map $q: S^n \to \mathbb {RP}^n$, which is a submersion because each point of $S^n$ is in the image of a smooth local section. Since $q$ and $\pi $ are constant on each other's fibers, Proposition A.19 shows that there is a diffeomorphism $S^n/\Gamma \to \mathbb {RP}^n$, and $q$ is equal to the composition $S^n \to S^n/\Gamma \to \mathbb {RP}^n$. Since this is a smooth normal covering map followed by a diffeomorphism, $q$ is also a smooth normal covering map. Thus $S^n$ is the universal covering space of $\mathbb {RP}^n$, and the fundamental group of $\mathbb {RP}^n$ is isomorphic to $\{ \pm 1\} $. \end{example}
